s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal swelling with bilateral testicular enlargement
salient_findings: Large, solid masses in both testes on scrotal ultrasound
Tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
key_facts: Scrotal ultrasound showed large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were within normal limits
No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on PET-CT scan
Left radical inguinal orchiectomy was performed
Histologic examination demonstrated a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types

shortlist.label: Mixed germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types and lymphovascular invasion

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral testicular enlargement and solid masses on ultrasound

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular tumor with lymphovascular invasion and normal tumor markers

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with small, medium, and large cells

shortlist.label: Spermatocytic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular tumor with distinct cell types and absence of lymphadenopathy

raw.rationale: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor with three distinct cell types and lymphovascular invasion, along with normal tumor markers, is more consistent with a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, which can be composed of multiple cell types and often presents with aggressive features.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas are typically uniform in cell type and less likely to have the pleomorphic appearance described.

rejected.label: Mixed germ cell tumor
rejected.why: While mixed germ cell tumors can have multiple cell types, the term is broader and the specific details provided do not necessitate this diagnosis over non-seminomatous germ cell tumor.

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: Embryonal carcinoma is a subtype of non-seminomatous germ cell tumor but the description does not specifically point to this subtype alone.

rejected.label: Spermatocytic tumor
rejected.why: Spermatocytic tumors are rare and typically have a distinct histological appearance that does not match the pleomorphic description given.
